arxiv-2104-10710.title: Lifshitz hydrodynamics at generic z from a moving black brane
arxiv-2104-10710.creator: Aruna Rajagopal, Larus Thorlacius
arxiv-2104-10710.description: Abstract A Lifshitz black brane at generic dynamical critical exponent z > 1 z>1 , with non-zero linear momentum along the boundary, provides a holographic dual description of a non-equilibrium steady state in a quantum critical fluid, with Lifshitz scale invariance but without boost symmetry.

arxiv-2207-14152.title: Quantization for the mixtures of overlap probability distributions
arxiv-2207-14152.creator: 1 Asha Barua, 2 Angelina Chavera, 3 Ivan Djordjevic, 4 Valerie Manzano, 5 Sergio Soto Quintero, 6 Mrinal Kanti Roychowdhury, 7 Hilda Tejeda
arxiv-2207-14152.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by 1 Asha Barua, 2 Angelina Chavera, 3 Ivan Djordjevic, 4 Valerie Manzano, 5 Sergio Soto Quintero, 6 Mrinal Kanti Roychowdhury, 7 Hilda Tejeda. Mixtures of probability distributions, also known as mixed distributions, are an exciting new area for optimal quantization. In this paper, we have considered a mixed distribution which is generated by overlap uniform distributions. For this mixed distribution we determine the optimal sets of n n -means and the n n th quantization errors for all positive integers n n .

arxiv-2305-11835.title: Contact Optimization with Learning from Demonstration: Application in Long-term Non-prehensile Planar Manipulation
arxiv-2305-11835.creator: Teng Xue, Sylvain Calinon
arxiv-2305-11835.description: Abstract Long-term non-prehensile planar manipulation is a challenging task for planning and control, requiring determination of both continuous and discrete contact configurations, such as contact points and modes. This leads to the non-convexity and hybridness of contact optimization. To overcome these difficulties, we propose a novel approach that incorporates human demonstrations into trajectory optimization.

arxiv-2402-18757.title: Difficult control is related to instability in biologically inspired Boolean networks
arxiv-2402-18757.creator: Bryan C. Daniels, Enrico Borriello
arxiv-2402-18757.description: Abstract Abstract Previous work in Boolean dynamical networks has suggested that the number of components that must be controlled to select an existing attractor is typically set by the number of attractors admitted by the dynamics, with no dependence on the size of the network.

arxiv-2406-12777.title: Medvedev degrees of subshifts on groups
arxiv-2406-12777.creator: Sebastián Barbieri, Nicanor Carrasco-Vargas
arxiv-2406-12777.description: Abstract The Medvedev degree of a subshift is a dynamical invariant of computable origin that can be used to compare the complexity of subshifts that contain only uncomputable configurations. We develop theory to describe how these degrees can be transferred from one group to another through algebraic and geometric relations, such as quotients, subgroups, translation-like actions and quasi-isometries.

arxiv-2501-07236.title: CSTA : Spatial-Temporal Causal Adaptive Learning for Exemplar-Free Video Class-Incremental Learning
arxiv-2501-07236.creator: Tieyuan Chen, Huabin Liu, Chern Hong Lim, John See, Xing Gao, Junhui Hou, Weiyao Lin
arxiv-2501-07236.description: Abstract Continual learning aims to acquire new knowledge while retaining past information. Class-incremental learning (CIL) presents a challenging scenario where classes are introduced sequentially. For video data, the task becomes more complex than image data because it requires learning and preserving both spatial appearance and temporal action involvement.

arxiv-2504-20780.title: Deterministic Dynamic Maximal Matching in Sublinear Update Time
arxiv-2504-20780.creator: Aaron Bernstein, Sayan Bhattacharya, Peter Kiss, Thatchaphol Saranurak
arxiv-2504-20780.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Aaron Bernstein, Sayan Bhattacharya, Peter Kiss, Thatchaphol Saranurak. arxiv-2602-08400.title: SCOUT-RAG: Scalable and Cost-Efficient Unifying Traversal for Agentic Graph-RAG over Distributed Domains
arxiv-2602-08400.creator: Longkun Li, Yuanben Zou, Jinghan Wu, Yuqing Wen, Jing Li Hangwei Qian, Ivor Tsang
arxiv-2602-08400.description: Abstract Graph-RAG improves LLM reasoning using structured knowledge, yet conventional designs rely on a centralized knowledge graph. In distributed and access-restricted settings (e.g., hospitals or multinational organizations), retrieval must select relevant domains and appropriate traversal depth without global graph visibility or exhaustive querying.

pmc-10499994.title: Global fossil fuel reduction pathways under different climate mitigation strategies and ambitions
pmc-10499994.creator: Ploy Achakulwisut, Peter Erickson, Céline Guivarch, Roberto Schaeffer, Elina Brutschin, Steve Pye
pmc-10499994.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The mitigation scenarios database of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change’s Sixth Assessment Report is an important resource for informing policymaking on energy transitions. However, there is a large variety of models, scenario designs, and resulting outputs. Here we analyse the scenarios consistent with limiting warming to 2 °C or below regarding the speed, trajectory, and feasibility of different fossil fuel reduction pathways.

pmc-11414835.creator: Ming Hu, Feng-Ying Ye, Wei Yu, Kang Sheng, Zhi-Rong Xu, Jin-Jin Fu, Xin Wen, Hai-Tao Feng, Minghua Liu, Yan-Song Zheng

However, no matter whether helical molecules or helical aggregates, they usually display modest chiroptical signals, which limits their practical applications.

pmc-11476651.title: Improving Therapy for Children with Scoliosis through Reducing Ionizing Radiation by Using Alternative Imaging Methods—A Study Protocol
pmc-11476651.creator: Fee Keil, Robert Schneider, Nenad Polomac, Omar Zabar, Tobias Finger, Fabian Holzgreve, Marcus Czabanka, Christina Erbe, David A Groneberg, Elke Hattingen, Daniela Ohlendorf, Panagiotis Diaremes, Panagiotis G Korovessis, Gonzalo Mariscal

The aim of this study was to find out whether primary diagnosis, including surgical planning, could be carried out entirely without computed tomography (CT) scans and whether follow-up could be replaced with alternative methods without the use of X-rays.

pmc-11481244.title: Association between serum IgM and all-cause mortality risk in Chinese centenarians: a prospective cohort study
pmc-11481244.creator: Weiguang Zhang, Yuting Duan, Zhe Li, Yue Niu, Bin Wang, Zhe Feng, Ding Sun, Hao Li, Zehao Zhang, Zeyu Qu, Miao Liu, Hongyan Hu, Qiao Zhu, Yujian Chen, Chaoxue Ning, Shihui Fu, Shanshan Yang, Shengshu Wang, Yali Zhao, Yao He, Xiangmei Chen, Yizhi Chen
pmc-11481244.description: BackgroundWe investigated the associations between IgM, IgG, IgA, and IgE levels and all-cause mortality risk in Chinese centenarians.MethodsAll participants were from the China Hainan Centenarian Cohort Study. Eligible participants were divided into quartiles based on their IgM, IgG, IgA, and IgE levels.

pmc-11493966.title: Decoding the multiple functions of ZBP1 in the mechanism of sepsis-induced acute lung injury
pmc-11493966.creator: Ting Gong, Yu Fu, Qingde Wang, Patricia A Loughran, Yuehua Li, Timothy R Billiar, Zongmei Wen, Youtan Liu, Jie Fan
pmc-11493966.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Sepsis-induced acute lung injury (ALI), characterized by severe hypoxemia and pulmonary leakage, remains a leading cause of mortality in intensive care units. The exacerbation of ALI during sepsis is largely attributed to uncontrolled inflammatory responses and endothelial dysfunction. Emerging evidence suggests an important role of Z-DNA binding protein 1 (ZBP1) as a sensor in innate immune to drive inflammatory signaling and cell death during infections. However, the role of ZBP1 in sepsis-induced ALI has yet to be defined.

pmc-11544309.title: A new species of Rhopalopsole (Plecoptera, Leuctridae) from Yunnan Province, China
pmc-11544309.creator: Xiao Yang, Yu-Zhou Du
pmc-11544309.description: BackgroundA new species of the genus Rhopalopsole (Plecoptera, Leuctridae) from Yunnan Province, China, Rhopalopsoledulongjianga sp. nov., is described and illustrated.New informationThis new species is compared to the similar species, Rhopalopsolebispina (Wu, 1949). Additionally, we provide a supplemental description and colour plates of R.bispina. A key to Rhopalopsole species from Yunnan Province, China, is also provided in this paper.

pmc-12521703.title: Timelygpt: extrapolatable transformer pre-training for long-term time-series forecasting in healthcare
pmc-12521703.creator: Ziyang Song, Qincheng Lu, Hao Xu, Ziqi Yang, He Zhu, David Buckeridge, Yue Li
pmc-12521703.description: PurposeLarge-scale pre-trained models (PTMs) such as BERT and GPT have recently achieved great success in Natural Language Processing and Computer Vision domains. However, the development of PTMs on healthcare time-series data is lagging behind. This underscores the limitations of the existing transformer-based architectures, particularly their scalability to handle large-scale time series and ability to capture long-term temporal dependencies.

pmc-12617387.title: The Reporting and Methodological Recommendations for Observational Studies Estimating the Effects of Deprescribing Medications (REMROSE‐D) ISPE‐Endorsed Guidance
pmc-12617387.creator: Kaleen N Hayes, Joshua D Niznik, Danijela Gnjidic, Frank Moriarty, Dimitri Bennett, Marie‐Laure Laroche, Denis Talbot, Matthew Alcusky, Maurizio Sessa, Antoinette B Coe, Caroline Sirois, Andrew R Zullo, Xiaojuan Li, Sri Harsha Chalasani, Jehath Syed, Mouna Sawan, Daniela C Moga
pmc-12617387.description: PurposePharmacoepidemiologic studies on deprescribing are challenging to implement, yet little guidance exists on methods to avoid bias and minimum reporting for replicability and appraisal. We developed consensus recommendations for the methods and reporting of observational studies that aim to examine the effects of deprescribing.MethodsWe formed candidate recommendations based on our prior systematic review that methodologically appraised observational studies on deprescribing.

pmc-12718279.title: Neurodevelopmental and Psychosocial Outcomes in Adolescence of Children with Early Diagnoses of ADHD, Autism, Dyscalculia and Dyslexia
pmc-12718279.creator: Yufei Cai, Joni Holmes, Giorgia Michelini, Thalia C. Eley, Susan E. Gathercole
pmc-12718279.description: The study examined neurodevelopmental and psychosocial outcomes in adolescents aged 12 and 16 with childhood diagnoses of ADHD, autism, dyscalculia, or dyslexia. Participants were drawn from the Twins Early Development Study based on parent-reported diagnoses between ages 7 and 9 of ADHD (n = 54), autism (n = 50), dyscalculia (n = 282), and dyslexia (n = 695).

pmc-12997122.title: A methodology for integrating AI into embodied human intelligence for the performance of complex tasks
pmc-12997122.creator: Tamim Ahmed, Thanassis Rikakis
pmc-12997122.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). We propose a theory and methodology for designing human-artificial intelligence (AI) collaboration in complex, embodied tasks. The theory distinguishes human embodied intelligence from computational intelligence and identifies synergies in which AI enhances—rather than replicates or replaces—human performance. We represent observable structures of expert performance as a nested network with four interdependent layers: Environment (space and tools), Activity (what is done), Goals (what is aimed for), and Meaning (how performance is interpreted), all connected by dynamic four-layer edges.

pmc-13299708.title: Cross-Sectional Mediation Analysis: How Registered Nurses’ Knowledge, Attitude, and Practice Influence Adherence to Pressure Injury Prevention

pmc-13299708.description: Background: Pressure injuries (PIs) remain a major and escalating global patient safety concern, affecting 12.8% of hospitalized patients worldwide and contributing to rising prevalence and mortality rates from 5.63 to 8.18 and 0.31 to 0.47 per 100,000 population, respectively. The economic burden of PIs is substantial, amounting to $26.

pmc-13346097.title: Differential Cognitive Strategies for Speech-in-Noise Perception: A Comparative Study Between Yoga Practitioners and Non-practitioners
pmc-13346097.creator: Shrinidhi Devarahalli Manoj, Srikar Vijayasarathy, Vishal Kooknoor
pmc-13346097.description: BackgroundSpeech perception in noise varies widely even among normal-hearing individuals and is strongly influenced by cognitive factors such as attention, working memory and linguistic abilities. Yoga is known to enhance these domains, yet its potential impact on speech-in-noise perception remains insufficiently explored.

pmc-13392913.title: Assessment of the feed additive consisting of bentonite (dioctahedral montmorillonite) as an anticaking agent for all animal species and as a substance for reduction of the contamination of feed by mycotoxins for pigs, poultry and ruminants for the renewal of its authorisation (BASF SE)

pmc-13493546.title: Exploring the effectiveness and safety of stem cell therapy for repair of cartilage defects: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
pmc-13493546.creator: Mingjing Zhang, Simin Ni, Liqi Ng, Mo Zhou, Jianping Zhang, Nan Tao, Swastina Nath Varma, Aleksandra Ivanova, Rikin Hargunani, Yanwei Du, Chaozong Liu
pmc-13493546.description: BackgroundOsteoarthritis (OA) is one of the most common degenerative joint diseases worldwide, characterized by chronic pain, functional impairment, and progressive cartilage loss. Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) therapy has emerged as a promising regenerative strategy due to its chondrogenic and immunomodulatory properties.

pmc-13535857.title: Celiac Disease Emerging After ASCT in Multiple Myeloma: A Rare Diagnostic Intersection and Literature Review
pmc-13535857.creator: Mais Musleh, Mahmoud Alhamadeh Alswij, Qossay Alhusein, Kalyani Sen
pmc-13535857.description: BackgroundAutologous stem cell transplantation (ASCT) is a standard component of therapy for eligible patients with multiple myeloma. Persistent gastrointestinal symptoms after ASCT are commonly attributed to infection, medication‐related toxicity, or disease relapse, whereas autoimmune enteropathies such as celiac disease are rarely considered.

pmc-13623961.title: Calcium-tolerant electrode strategy for efficient hydrogen peroxide electrosynthesis in natural water
pmc-13623961.creator: Ke Wang, Ying Zhu, Yuan Yao, Ke Wang
pmc-13623961.description: Calcium scaling is traditionally regarded as a major impediment to the practical application of decentralized H2O2 electrosynthesis via two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e− ORR). Herein, we demonstrate that the calcium scale unexpectedly enhances H2O2 electroproduction. Dissolved Ca2+, rather than precipitated scale, is the dominant factor suppressing H2O2 electrosynthesis.

pmc-13634011.title: Taking the Right to Die Seriously
pmc-13634011.creator: Konrad Szocik, Matti Häyry, Pawel Januszewicz
pmc-13634011.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This article offers a Hohfeldian analysis of the right to die and asks what follows, normatively and institutionally, once the relevant incidents are distinguished. It argues that debates about assisted dying frequently conflate four questions: whether choosing death is morally permitted (licence), whether others must not interfere with that choice (negative claim-right), whether a valid request can alter others’ normative situation (normative power), and whether anyone owes assistance (positive claim-right).
